why: The first still and clip had a second Brandon under the sink.
still: A photograph from a lens fixed high on a bathroom wall, looking down at a cramped bathroom where a narrow cupboard door under the basin stands open. Brandon, the only person in the room, kneels upright on a dry lino floor in front of the open cupboard with his whole body and face in clear view. One arm reaches into the cupboard and holds a spanner on a chrome isolation valve, and a small torch is clamped in his teeth. His brows are lifted and his eyes are crinkled with delight. The cupboard interior holds only pipes. The floor is dry and the colours are washed out. A single overhead strip light lights the room. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon eases the spanner a quarter turn on the chrome valve, pauses and peers at the pipe. Afterwards he lets go of the spanner, lifts one thumb beside his face and his eyes crinkle. The overhead strip light hums. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Metal on metal, a faint tick of pipework, a quiet pleased exhale through the nose. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

why: The first clip's ambulance became a white van marked POLICE and swung round.
still: A photograph from a lens fixed at the top of a lamp post, looking down steeply at a suburban British street in flat overcast daylight. Brandon jogs along the pavement, small and foreshortened from above, in a loose grey tracksuit and with an easy, upright stride, his face turned forward and calm. In the road beside him an ambulance, bright yellow with a green and yellow chequered side stripe, a blue light bar on its roof and plain panels free of lettering, rolls slowly the same way he is running, and Sophie sits in the passenger window looking out at him with her brows drawn together and her mouth closed. Wet tarmac, a postbox and parked cars give washed-out, compressed colour. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon jogs steadily along the pavement and away down the street while the yellow ambulance creeps forward in a straight line beside him, always facing the same way. Sophie's head turns a little to keep watching him through the window. Its blue roof lights stay unlit. A leaf spins along the gutter. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Rhythmic running footfalls, a low diesel engine idle, tyres on wet tarmac, a distant dog bark. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

why: Jack asked for bloody shoes; the first still's trainers only looked grubby.
still: A photorealistic wide frame of a small, hard-surfaced coroner's examination room, taken from a lens on a wall bracket above the door and looking down across the room. A stainless steel table stands in the centre of the frame with a body under a white sheet, and a pair of white trainers hangs out of the end of the sheet, their toes and laces soaked dark red with blood, a smear of the same red on the steel beneath them. Giles stands beside the table on the right of the frame, his head slightly lowered and his brows drawn together, one finger pressed to his ear and his lips moving as though speaking quietly into the air, his eyes aimed at the floor. Pale tiled walls, a steel sink, a wall clock with blank hands and a trolley of covered trays recede behind him. The light is hard fluorescent strip light with cold green-white reflections on the steel, producing a washed-out picture with compression blocks, grain and slightly blown highlights on the table. No readable writing or numbers anywhere in frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Giles beside the steel table keeps one finger pressed to his ear and his lips move softly, while his gaze stays on the floor. Afterwards he shifts his weight onto his other foot and his eyes lift briefly to the trainers before dropping again. A fluorescent tube flickers faintly over the sink. The camera does not move. Audio: the buzz of a fluorescent tube, a refrigeration unit humming, the squeak of a rubber sole on tile, a slow drip from the sink. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.
